_comment: Real-error validation via published Matters Arising (third-party expert ground truth). This is METHOD CALIBRATION, not detector performance. The headline is the discipline: near-zero false positives and a declarable boundary. The 25% is the honest sensitivity of a GENERAL-REASONING auditor on real domain errors — it keeps the synthetic 88% honest, it is not the product's accuracy. reproduce.py recomputes every value from the anonymized per-target CSVs. n=7 is tiny by design (each target is a real, formally-refuted error); nothing here reaches significance, and nothing reaches VALIDATED without the external inter-nature axis.

specificity.note: cross-domain decoys; independently confirmed across two blind adjudicators

boundary.note: the lens lands only on defects reconstructible from the text by general reasoning (arithmetic, internal contradiction, definitional entailment); it misses defects that need domain re-derivation or external data — the declared out-of-scope class

sensitivity_calibration.note: real P-class recall 1/4 vs synthetic 88% (see benchmarks/calibration): the synthetic→real drop is the honest calibration, not noise
